title: Demonstrationes circa residua ex divisione potestatum per numeros primos resultantia

deep.reconstruction:
Context: E449 studies the residues of the geometric progression 1, a, a^2, ... modulo a prime P. Its later aim, beyond this page, is to show that some a, which Euler calls a 'radix primitiva', produces all P-1 nonzero residues.

§8: Numbers are sorted into classes ('ordines') by their remainder mod P (set up in §6-7 on the previous page). Any member mP+ε of a class determines the class as well as its least member ε, so a residue may be denoted by any representative. In modern terms, residues are elements of Z/PZ and any lift represents them.

§9: Negative representatives ε-P, ε-2P, ... are also allowed. If ε > P/2 then |ε-P| < P/2. So every residue can be written with absolute value at most P/2; for odd P this is at most (P-1)/2. This is the system of least absolute residues.

Observationes §10: Whether all numbers below P occur among the residues of a^k depends on a. For a=1 every residue is 1. For a=P-1 the residues are 1, P-1, 1, P-1, ..., that is +1, -1, +1, -1, ... In modern terms, the order of a ranges from 1 to P-1, and P-1 ≡ -1 has order 2.

§11: Example P=7, a=3. The residues of 3^k are 1, 3, 2, 6, 4, 5, 1, ..., so 3 is a primitive root mod 7 (order 6).

The page is preparatory: definitions and examples leading to the study of the period of a^k mod P and to Euler's proposed (incomplete) existence proof of primitive roots later in the paper.
errors: No mathematical errors. Minor caveat: §9's bound 'not exceeding half of P' is stated for a general prime P. For P=2 it is trivial; for odd P the bound is (P-1)/2. In §10 the claim that a=P-1 gives the alternating series ±1 is correct for P>2.

ideas.what: Partition of the integers into P classes by remainder; any member of a class can represent the residue
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Disquisitiones Arithmeticae, 1801) for the congruence notation; the idea is implicit in Euler and earlier writers
ideas.where_published: Euler E262 (Theoremata circa residua ex divisione potestatum relicta) and E449 itself

ideas.what: Using negative representatives so that every residue has absolute value at most P/2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Disquisitiones, art. 4, 'residua minima absoluta'); Euler uses the idea earlier
ideas.where_published: E449 (Novi Commentarii 18); unsure about earlier Euler papers

ideas.what: The residues of a^k mod P may or may not exhaust 1..P-1 depending on a; examples a=1, a=P-1, and 3 mod 7
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (the term 'radix primitiva' is introduced in E449); existence proof by Gauss (and Legendre)

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary definitions and worked examples of residue classes, least absolute residues and a primitive root mod 7. All are well documented in the history of Euler's number theory and in E449's known role.
transcription_corrections: Transcription is essentially accurate. The scan reads 'deaotetur', a print or scan artifact for 'denotetur', which the transcription already renders correctly.
The exponents 3^2 to 3^9 in the progression in §11 are faint in the scan but correctly transcribed. The residue sequence 1, 3, 2, 6, 4, 5, 1, 3, 2, 6 checks out arithmetically.
